technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring XD module development guidelines for all new modules (source, sink).

For U1, implement a generic JDBC source module that can read from any database with a JDBC driver, and a configurable HDFS/HAWQ/GPDB sink module that supports writing to HDFS, HAWQ, and Greenplum (GPDB) via appropriate connectors (e.g., HDFS via Hadoop FS, HAWQ/GPDB via JDBC).
For U2, conduct a spike on Kafka simple consumer API (low-level) using Kafka 0.9.x client libraries; document findings, approach, and next steps for future implementation.
For U3, extend Spring XD admin server with a REST endpoint (multipart file upload) to accept uber-jar custom modules and register them in the module registry.
For U5 and U6, create new source and sink modules with command-line options as specified (generator: --numMsgs, --msgSize, --numThreads; perf-meter: --numMsgs).
For U7, use Spring XD singlenode container to deploy the stream 'generator | perf-meter' and measure performance characteristics (throughput, latency).
For U8, write unit and integration tests for existing Kafka source and sink modules using Spring XD test support and embedded Kafka; integrate tests into CI pipeline (e.g., Jenkins, Travis).
All modules will be built as Maven projects and packaged as uber-jars for deployment.
Code reviews and documentation updates will follow the project's contribution guidelines.
assumptions: The development environment already has Spring XD source code checked out and builds successfully.
The team is familiar with Spring XD module development, Spring Framework, and Kafka.
Kafka version is 0.9.x (compatible with Spring XD at the time).
HAWQ and GPDB can be accessed via JDBC drivers; HDFS access uses Hadoop FileSystem API.
The REST API for module deployment will be added to the Spring XD admin server and secured appropriately (basic auth or OAuth2).
The sample GitHub project (U4) will be a separate repository with a README, sample configuration files, and a simple stream definition.
Performance testing (U7) will be executed on a local singlenode container; no distributed cluster setup is required.
Test coverage for Kafka source and sink (U8) assumes the modules already exist (from previous work) and only test code is needed.
CI infrastructure (e.g., Jenkins) is already configured; only test job configuration is needed.
Effort estimates are for a single developer with moderate Spring XD experience.
